examGuide.title: Mental model and derivation
examGuide.body:
ARQ combines acknowledgments, sequence numbers and retransmission. Stop-and-wait permits one outstanding frame, so long RTT can dominate utilization. Go-Back-N retransmits a suffix while selective repeat can retransmit individual frames. Sequence-number wrap requires limiting windows: standard selective repeat needs sender/receiver windows no larger than half the sequence space to distinguish old from new frames. Timeout and ACK assumptions determine exact traces.

**Key relationship:** Stop-and-wait utilization≈Ttrans/(Ttrans+2Tprop), ignoring ACK time and errors

examGuide.title: A repeatable solving procedure
examGuide.body:
1. Draw frame/ACK timelines.
2. Identify retransmission policy.
3. Check window versus sequence-space constraints.

examGuide.title: Approach the exam question
examGuide.body: Stop-and-wait utilization with negligible ACK transmission is Ttx/(Ttx+2Tprop). Sliding windows need enough outstanding frames to cover the ACK round trip: ceil(1+2Tprop/Ttx). Sequence-space requirements differ for go-back-N and selective repeat, so specify the protocol rather than applying one window rule universally.

examGuide.title: Worked problem
examGuide.body:
Frame transmission takes 2 ms; one-way propagation is 9 ms. What minimum sliding-window size achieves full utilization with negligible ACK and processing times?

**Answer: 10.** The first ACK returns after 2+2·9=20 ms. Sending ten frames occupies those 20 ms. Wmin=ceil(1+18/2)=10 frames.

examGuide.title: Conditions and edge cases
examGuide.body:
With losses, retransmissions reduce achieved utilization. This ideal calculation assumes a lossless link and sufficient sequence space.

A window-size bound depends on the specific ARQ protocol and receiver behavior.

examGuide.title: Worked question patterns
examGuide.body:
#### Pattern 1 · MCQ

With m sequence bits, standard selective-repeat maximum equal window size is:

- **A.** m
- **B.** 2ᵐ
- **C.** 2ᵐ−1
- **D.** 2ᵐ⁻¹

**Answer: D.** At most half the sequence space prevents old frames being mistaken for new ones after wraparound.

#### Pattern 2 · MSQ

Choose true statements.

- **A.** Stop-and-wait has at most one unacknowledged frame
- **B.** ARQ can recover from loss by retransmission
- **C.** Selective repeat always retransmits every later frame
- **D.** Sequence-number wrap matters

**Answer: A, B, D.** Selective repeat targets individual missing frames; Go-Back-N retransmits a suffix.

#### Pattern 3 · NAT

Transmission time 1 ms, round-trip propagation 9 ms, negligible ACK size. Ideal stop-and-wait utilization?



**Answer: 0.1.** A cycle lasts 1+9=10 ms and sends for 1 ms. Utilization=1/10=0.1.

examGuide.title: Work through the supplied PYQs
examGuide.body:
#### GATE 2023 CS · Q17 · MCQ

[Open the original question and try it](/#/lesson/flow-control-arq?tab=practice)

**What is tested:** Link flow control and ARQ. Refer to the original image for complete givens and diagrams.

1. With negligible ACK transmission time, stop-and-wait utilization is Ttx/(Ttx+2Tprop)=1/(1+2Tprop/Ttx).
2. A longer link increases propagation time. A higher transmission rate reduces the time to send a fixed packet. Both increase the ratio Tprop/Ttx.
3. Utilization is therefore lowest for a **longer link and higher rate**, option B.

#### GATE 2025 CS2 · Q36 · MCQ

[Open the original question and try it](/#/lesson/flow-control-arq?tab=practice)

**What is tested:** Link flow control and ARQ. Refer to the original image for complete givens and diagrams.

1. Frame transmission time=3000/2000=1.5 s. The propagation delay is one-way 0.1 s, so round-trip propagation is 0.2 s. ACK transmission and processing are negligible.
2. A stop-and-wait cycle lasts 1.5+0.2=1.7 s, with 1.5 s carrying data.
3. Utilization=1.5/1.7×100≈**88.23%, A**.
